title: Randomized Coordinate Descent Methods
text:
The Reality of Modern Data

In recent years, we can observe an increasing interest to optimization problems of a very big size.
We are talking in the scale of millions!
Traditional methods require evaluating the entire gradient vector to find the exact steepest descent.


Evaluating \(\nabla f(x)\) becomes computationally expensive

title: Randomized Coordinate Descent Methods
text:
Nesterov’s Insight



“We must adopt an optimization technique based on the random partial update of decision variables.”

title: Randomized Coordinate Descent Methods
text:
The Main Idea – Coordinate Relaxation
Instead of updating all coordinates at once, update only one block of coordinates per iteration.


Partition \(\mathbb{R}^N\) into \(n\) blocks



\[x = ( x^{(1)}, x^{(2)}, ..., x^{(n)} )\]



At each step, pick a random block \(i_k\)​ and move only that block.



If each coordinate update is cheap (e.g., sparse data), many cheap steps can outperform a few expensive full‑gradient steps.

title: Randomized Coordinate Descent Methods
text:
Sparse Quadratic Problem

\[f(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} f_i(x^{(i)}) + \frac{1}{2} \| Ax-b \|^2 \]


\(f_i\) are convex differentiable univariate functions
Each column \(a_i\)​ of \(A\) is sparse, each with \(p_i\) number of non-zero elements.


\[x_+ = x + \alpha a_i \]



Only requires \(O(p_i)\) steps to compute



Nesterov’s insight can be thousands of times faster per effective pass.

title: Randomized Coordinate Descent Methods
section: The Problem we are Trying to Solve
text:
The Problem we are Trying to Solve

\[ \min_{x \in \mathbb{R}^N} f(x) \]


\(f\) is convex and differentiable
Optimal set \(X^*\) is nonempty and bounded

title: Randomized Coordinate Descent Methods
text:
Mathematical Notation

\[ \langle x,y \rangle = \sum_{i=1}^n x^{(i)}y^{(i)} \]


\[ \| s \|^*  = \max_{\| h\| = 1} \langle s,x\rangle\]


\[ s^\# \in arg\max_x \; [\langle s,x\rangle - \frac{1}{2}\| x\|^2]\]

title: Randomized Coordinate Descent Methods
text:
Coordinate‑wise Smoothness
We assume each partial gradient is Lipschitz in its own block

\[ \| f_i^\prime(x + U_ih_i) - f_i^\prime(x) \|^*_{(i)} \le L_i \| h_i \|_{(i)} \]


\(f_i^\prime(x)\) is the gradient w.r.t block \(i\)
\(L_i\) is the Lipschitz constant for block \(i\) (known or estimated)
\(\| \cdot \|_{(i)}\) is a norm we can choose per block

title: Randomized Coordinate Descent Methods
text:
Quadratic Upper Bound
From the Lipschitz condition, for any step \(h_i\)​ in block \(i\)

\[ f(x+ U_ih_i) \le f(x) + \langle f_i^\prime(x), h_i \rangle + \frac{L_i}{2} \| h_i \|^2_{(i)} \]


Block‑wise descent lemma

title: Randomized Coordinate Descent Methods
text:
Optimal Coordinate Step
We choose \(h_i\)​ to minimize the right‑hand side

\[ h^*_i = -\frac{1}{L_i} f_i^\prime(x)^\#\]


We can now define the optimal coordinate steps as


\[ T_i(x) = x - \frac{1}{L_i}U_if_i^\prime(x)^\# \]

title: Randomized Coordinate Descent Methods
text:
Guaranteed Decrease

\[ f(x) - f(T_i(x)) \ge \frac{1}{2L_i} (\| f_i^\prime(x) \|^*_{i})^2 \]


So the decrease is proportional to the squared size of the partial gradient.

title: Randomized Coordinate Descent Methods
text:
Random Coordinate Selection
At each iteration we pick a random block \(i\) with probability

\[ p_{\alpha}^i = \frac{L_i^\alpha}{\sum_{j=1}^n L_j^\alpha} \; ,\alpha \in \mathbb{R} \]

title: Randomized Coordinate Descent Methods
text:
RCD Algorithm


Input: starting point \(x_0\), parameter \(\alpha\)


For \(k=0,1,2,\dots\) do



Choose random block \(\color{#000000}{i_k}\) with probability \(p_\alpha(i)\)




Update: \[x_{k+1} = x_k - \frac{1}{L_{\color{#000000}{i_k}}} U_{\color{#000000}{i_k}} (f'_{\color{#000000}{i_k}}(x_k))^\#\]



End
